mainTopic: When does a payment to a זונה count as אתנן, and a challenge to רבי יוחנן's ruling about שביעית
overview: The גמרא asks why a payment given to a זונה before the act does not become forbidden as אתנן once the act happens. רבי אליעזר answers that she offered it as a קרבן before the act. The גמרא shows this works only in a middle case: he left the animal with her until the act, but let her acquire it right away if she needed it. רב הושעיא then asks whether merely consecrating the animal before the act is enough, and the question ends in תיקו. Next, two ברייתות contradict each other about a payment given after the act. רב חסדא explains that a specific named lamb is אתנן even if given later, while an unspecified lamb is not. The גמרא solves the problem of missing משיכה in one of two ways: either she is a non-Jew, or the lamb stands in her חצר and was set up as an אפותיקי. Finally, רב ששת returns to רבי יוחנן's ruling about borrowing produce during שביעית and begins an objection from a ברייתא about workers given a דינר; the objection continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Shouldn't the payment become forbidden retroactively?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling permitting a payment given before the act.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the prohibition of אתנן take effect on it retroactively!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא that allowed a payment handed over before the act. When the act later happens, the payment should turn into אתנן looking backward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The payment was given in exchange for the act. So once the act takes place, it seems the payment should become forbidden as אתנן going back in time. If so, how can the ברייתא permit it?

keyTerms.meaning: A prostitute's payment, which is forbidden as a קרבן

phrases.english: Let the prohibition of a prostitute's payment take effect on it retroactively!

steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא permitting a payment given before the act
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Payment given for a future act should become אתנן retroactively once the act happens.

steps.title: She already offered it before the act
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר explains that the ברייתא means she sacrificed the payment before the act happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: It is when she went ahead and sacrificed it first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers that the ברייתא is talking about a case where she already offered the animal as a קרבן before the act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the animal has already been offered, the later act cannot go back and make it forbidden. The retroactive prohibition has nothing left to take hold of.

keyTerms.meaning: She went first, did it beforehand
She offered it as a קרבן

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
When she went ahead and sacrificed it first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The payment would become forbidden retroactively.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since it was already offered before the act, the later act cannot make it forbidden.

steps.title: If he gave it to her outright, why teach it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case looks like, and shows the first option is too obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he told her 'Acquire it from now,' it is obviously permitted, since it is not his payment at the time of the act. It is just a gift he gave her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly רבי אליעזר's case is. It tries the first option and shows it is too obvious to need teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she owned the animal fully from the start, it was a plain gift and not tied to the act at all. Everyone already knows a gift is allowed, so the ברייתא would not need to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquire it for yourself from now

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If he said to her: 'Acquire it for yourself from now' —
it is obvious that it is permitted,
since it is not there at the time of the act,
phrases.notes: He means it no longer exists as a payment by then; it already became hers earlier.

phrases.english: and it is merely a gift that he gave her!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי אִי דְּאָמַר לַהּ קְנַי לִיךְ מֵעַכְשָׁיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Probes the case רבי אליעזר described
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Exactly what ownership arrangement makes רבי אליעזר's case work

steps.title: If she does not own it, she cannot offer it
steps.stepSummary: The second option fails: without ownership she cannot consecrate the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he did not tell her 'Acquire it from now,' how can she offer it? The Torah says 'And a man who consecrates his house as holy.' Just as his house is in his possession, so too anything consecrated must be in his possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the other option and shows it is impossible. If the animal is not yet hers, she has no right to make it a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about consecrating 'his house' teaches that a person can only consecrate what he owns. So if the animal still belongs to the man, her offering it would mean nothing. Both options seem to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrates, makes holy for the בית המקדש
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי דְּלָא אָמַר לַהּ ״קְנַי לִיךְ מֵעַכְשָׁיו״,
phrases.english: And if he did not say to her: 'Acquire it for yourself from now,'
how can she offer it?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'can she.'

phrases.english: 'And when a man shall consecrate his house as holy'
the Merciful One said,
just as his house is in his possession,
so too anything consecrated must be in his possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי דְּלָא אָמַר לַהּ קְנַי לִיךְ מֵעַכְשָׁיו הֵיכִי מָצְיָא מַקְרְבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the second option also fails, so both ways seem closed
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's case of her offering it first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person can only consecrate what he owns, so without ownership she cannot offer it.

steps.title: A middle case: hers only if she needs it now
steps.stepSummary: The case is where he left it with her until the act, but let her acquire it now if she needs it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he told her: 'Let it stay with you until the time of the act, and if you need it, acquire it from now.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the case that avoids both problems. It is a conditional arrangement between the two options.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the animal is meant as payment for the act, so it is not just an obvious gift. But since she may acquire it right away if she needs it, it counts as hers when she offers it. Because she offered it before the act, the אתנן prohibition never takes hold.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be with you, in your keeping

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's case works only with a middle arrangement. The animal is meant as payment, so the ruling is not obvious. Yet she may acquire it now if she needs it, so it is hers and she can consecrate it. Once it is offered before the act, אתנן cannot take hold.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how carefully the גמרא checks that a case is neither too obvious to teach nor impossible under the rules of ownership and הקדש.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he said to her:
'Let it be with you until the time of the act,
and if you need it, acquire it from now.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּאָמַר לַהּ לֶהֱוֵי גַּבִּיךְ עַד שְׁעַת בִּיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem from both options with a middle case
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He left it with her until the act, letting her acquire it now if she needs it; she then owns it and may offer it before the act.

steps.title: What if she only consecrated the animal before the act?
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא asks whether consecrating the payment before the act counts like sacrificing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא asks: if she first consecrated the animal, what is the law? Since the rule is that saying 'this is for הקדש' is like handing something to a person, maybe it counts as if she already sacrificed it. Or perhaps, since right now the animal is still standing here, it is still considered her payment?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא builds on the previous case of 'she sacrificed it first' and asks about a weaker case: she only consecrated it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying words of הקדש transfers ownership to the Temple, just as handing an item to a person does. So maybe the animal already left her hands, like a sacrificed animal. On the other hand, the animal still physically exists at the time of the act, so maybe it still counts as payment.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks a question he is unsure about
She consecrated it (declared it holy for the Temple)
His spoken declaration to the Temple
His handing over of an item to an ordinary person

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya asked:
If she first consecrated it, what is the law?
Since the Master said:
declaring something for the Most High is like handing it over to an ordinary person,
phrases.notes: Just saying the words makes it belong to the Temple. No physical handover is needed.

phrases.english: so it is as if she had sacrificed it,
or perhaps

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא מִיהָא הָא קָאֵי וְאִיתֵיהּ בְּעֵינֵיהּ?
phrases.english: now, at any rate, it is standing here and still exists intact?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי אליעזר's case of 'she sacrificed it first' to a case where she only consecrated it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does consecration alone, before the act, remove the animal from the status of a forbidden אתנן?

steps.title: Trying to answer from רבי אליעזר's exact wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי אליעזר's word 'sacrificed' implies that consecrating alone is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us answer this from רבי אליעזר, who said the case is where she sacrificed it first. That means only sacrificing helps, but consecrating does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רב הושעיא's question by reading closely what רבי אליעזר said in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר chose the word 'sacrificed,' not 'consecrated.' The suggestion is that he said it that way on purpose: if consecrating were enough, he would have said the easier case.

keyTerms.meaning: She sacrificed it on the altar
Specifically, exactly this and not more

phrases.english: Let us resolve it from Rabbi Eliezer,
for Rabbi Eliezer said: the case is where she sacrificed it first.
That means specifically where she sacrificed it,
but if she only consecrated it, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to רב הושעיא's question.
steps.raayaObject: That consecration alone does not remove the אתנן prohibition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exact wording of רבי אליעזר: 'she sacrificed it first'.

steps.title: The proof fails: רב הושעיא is asking about רבי אליעזר himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof, because רבי אליעזר's wording can be read two ways. The question remains unresolved (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא's question is about רבי אליעזר's own words. Is it obvious to רבי אליעזר that only sacrificing helps and consecrating does not, since the animal still exists at the time of the act? Or perhaps sacrificing was obvious to him, but he was unsure about consecrating? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: you cannot prove anything from רבי אליעזר, because his words are exactly what is in doubt. It ends with תיקו, meaning no answer was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read רבי אליעזר's choice of 'sacrificed.' Maybe he meant to exclude consecrating. Or maybe he only said the case he was sure about and left consecrating open. Since both readings work, the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He is in doubt about it
At the time of the act
Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Whether consecrating an animal before the act removes the אתנן prohibition is left as a תיקו. Only actually sacrificing it before the act clearly helps.
steps.confusionAlert: Saying 'דוקא' (only this case) does not always mean the other case is excluded. Sometimes the speaker just mentioned what he was sure of and stayed silent about the rest.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר גּוּפֵיהּ קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ, מַאי?
phrases.english: It is about Rabbi Eliezer's own statement that he is asking: what did he mean?
Is it clearly obvious to Rabbi Eliezer
that only if she sacrificed it is it permitted,
but if she consecrated it, no,
because it still exists at the time of the act?
Or perhaps 'she sacrificed it' is obvious to him,
while 'she consecrated it' he is unsure about?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר גּוּפֵיהּ קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from רבי אליעזר's wording and closes the question with תיקו.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference from רבי אליעזר's wording completely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wording 'sacrificed' may simply be the case he was sure of, not a deliberate exclusion of consecration.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תיקו: the status of a payment consecrated before the act remains in doubt.

steps.title: Two ברייתות contradict about payment given after the act
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא permits a payment given after the act, but another forbids it even three years later.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: if he was with her and afterward gave her payment, it is permitted. But a different ברייתא says: if he was with her and afterward gave her payment, even three years later, her payment is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a ruling from the ברייתא and points out that another ברייתא seems to say the opposite. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא seems to hold that a payment given after the act was not there during the act, so it is not an אתנן. The second ברייתא treats any later payment for the act as an אתנן, even years afterward. The same case gets opposite rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: Her harlot's payment, which is forbidden as an offering
And they set them against each other: a contradiction between sources

phrases.aramaic: בָּא עָלֶיהָ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָתַן לָהּ אֶתְנַנָּהּ
phrases.english: If he had relations with her and afterward gave her, her payment
is permitted.
But a contradiction was raised:

phrases.aramaic: בָּא עָלֶיהָ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָתַן לָהּ,
phrases.english: If he had relations with her and afterward gave her payment,
even from now until three years later,
her payment is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תיקו, the גמרא moves to the next clause of the ברייתא and raises a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that payment given after the act is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא rules that payment given after the act is forbidden, even three years later. The two sources directly contradict each other.

steps.title: A specific lamb versus an unspecified lamb
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא resolves the contradiction between the two ברייתות. Promising 'this lamb' makes it אתנן even if it is given later. Promising just 'a lamb' does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said in the name of רב חסדא: There is no contradiction. The ברייתא that forbids is where he said, 'Be with me for this lamb.' The ברייתא that permits is where he said, 'Be with me for a lamb,' without saying which one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 9 by saying each ברייתא is talking about a different kind of promise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he names a specific lamb, that lamb is tied to the act from the start, so it is אתנן even if she receives it years later. When he promises a lamb in general, no particular lamb is the payment at the time of the act. So the lamb he hands over later is not considered אתנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Payment given to a זונה, forbidden as a קרבן

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said that Rav Chisda said:
It is not difficult.
This one is where he said, 'Be with me for this lamb.'
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that forbids the lamb, even three years later.

phrases.english: That one is where he said to her, 'Be with me for a lamb,' without specifying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא is about a different kind of promise
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seem to argue about whether a later payment is אתנן
steps.terutzMaskana: A specific named lamb is אתנן even if given later. An unspecified lamb is not.

steps.title: She never acquired the specific lamb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what saying 'this lamb' accomplishes, since no act of acquisition was done.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when he says to her 'for this lamb,' what difference does that make? No משיכה was done!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's answer. Just naming the lamb should not make it hers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An object normally becomes someone's property only through a formal act of acquisition, such as משיכה (pulling it). Without that, 'this lamb' is still the man's at the time of the act. So it should be no different from an unspecified lamb.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? What difference does it make?
Pulling: a formal way of acquiring an animal or object

phrases.english: But when he says to her, 'for this lamb,'
what of it?
Pulling is missing!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אָמַר לַהּ ״בְּטָלֶה זֶה״ מַאי הָוֵי
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that naming a specific lamb makes it payment from the start
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without משיכה she never acquired the lamb, so naming it should change nothing

steps.title: A non-Jewish woman does not need pulling
steps.stepSummary: The case is a non-Jewish זונה, who does not acquire through משיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is a non-Jewish זונה, who does not acquire by pulling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: the ברייתא is about a non-Jewish woman, for whom משיכה is not the way of acquiring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משיכה is a way of acquiring that applies between Jews. A non-Jew acquires in a different way, so the lack of משיכה is no problem. The named lamb can count as tied to the act.

phrases.english: It is about a non-Jewish זונה,
who does not acquire by pulling.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a non-Jewish woman
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without משיכה the lamb could not be hers
steps.terutzMaskana: For a non-Jewish woman, משיכה is not the way she acquires, so the question falls away

steps.title: Or a Jewish woman with the lamb in her courtyard
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: the case is a Jewish זונה, and the lamb is already standing in her חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: really, it is about a Jewish זונה, and the lamb is standing in her courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to answer the question about משיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even for a Jewish woman no משיכה is needed if the lamb is in her own חצר. A person's courtyard acquires things for her. So naming 'this lamb' works.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: introduces another answer
Her courtyard, which can acquire things for her

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
really, it is about a Jewish זונה,
and where the lamb is standing in her courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 11, parallel to step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a lamb in her courtyard
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A Jewish woman would need משיכה
steps.terutzMaskana: Her חצר acquires the lamb for her, so no משיכה is needed

steps.title: Then she owned it before the act
steps.stepSummary: If the lamb was in her חצר, she owned it before the act. So it was not really 'given afterward.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If the lamb is standing in her courtyard, then how is this 'he was with her and afterward gave it to her'? She already acquired it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the courtyard answer. It no longer fits the ברייתא's case of payment given after the act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is discussing a payment given after the act. But with the lamb in her חצר, she acquired it as soon as he spoke, before the act. Then this is just a payment made in advance, not the case the ברייתא describes.

phrases.english: If it is standing in her courtyard,

phrases.aramaic: בָּא עָלֶיהָ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָתַן לָהּ,
phrases.english: how is this 'he was with her and afterward gave it to her'?
phrases.notes: He is quoting the case of the ברייתא from step 9.

phrases.english: She already acquired it!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If her חצר acquired the lamb immediately, the payment came before the act, which contradicts the ברייתא's case

steps.title: The lamb was set aside as a pledge
steps.stepSummary: The lamb in her חצר was only an אפותיקי, a security. It becomes her payment only if he fails to bring money by a deadline.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where he made the lamb a designated pledge for her. He said: 'If I bring you money by such-and-such a day, fine. If not, take the lamb as your payment.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves the courtyard answer. The lamb was only a pledge, so it becomes her payment only later, after the act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lamb is specific and already sits in her חצר, so no משיכה is needed. But it becomes her אתנן only when the deadline passes without money, which is after the act. This fits the ברייתא exactly: a named lamb that is given after the act, and it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case
A pledge set aside as security for a payment

steps.whatToRemember: A specific lamb promised as payment is אתנן even if she receives it later. The lack of משיכה is solved in one of two ways. Either she is a non-Jew, or the lamb stands in her חצר. In the חצר case, the lamb was set up as an אפותיקי, so it really becomes hers only after the act.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he made it a designated pledge for her,
where he said to her:
'If I bring you money
from now until such-and-such a day, fine,
phrases.notes: Meaning she gives the lamb back once he pays her the money.

phrases.english: and if not, take it as your payment.'

steps.terutzResolutionType: Refining the case with an אפותיקי arrangement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A lamb in her courtyard would be hers before the act
steps.terutzMaskana: As a pledge, the lamb becomes her payment only after the deadline, which is after the act, so the ברייתא fits

steps.title: רב ששת challenges from workers given a coin
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת begins an objection from a ברייתא. A man may tell his workers, 'Go eat and drink with this דינר,' and he need not worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת raised an objection: A person may say to his donkey drivers and his workers, 'Go and eat with this דינר,' 'Go out and drink with this דינר,' and he does not need to worry...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier topic: רבי יוחנן allowed borrowing produce from the poor during שביעית and repaying afterward. רב ששת starts challenging that ruling from a ברייתא. The ברייתא continues past this point, so this step is only setting up the objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes an employer handing his workers a coin to spend on food and drink. It says he need not be concerned about how they use it. The rest of the ברייתא, and the exact point of the challenge, come in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not need to worry

steps.confusionAlert: This is not part of the אתנן discussion. The גמרא has jumped back to the earlier topic of שביעית and רבי יוחנן's ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raised an objection:
A person may say to his donkey drivers and his workers,
'Go and eat with this דינר,'
'Go out and drink with this דינר,'
and he does not need to worry

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אתנן discussion and returns to the earlier topic of borrowing and repaying during שביעית
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that borrowing produce from the poor in שביעית and repaying later is allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Set up from a ברייתא about an employer giving his workers a coin. The full attack comes in the continuation of the ברייתא.
